name: Kalé Airport Cargo Community System at Miami International
summary: Miami International Airport announced at TIACA's Air Cargo Forum on October 27 that it has launched an AI-powered Airport Cargo Community System built by Kalé. MIA says it is now the busiest cargo hub in the world to use such a platform. The system gives MIA's freight forwarders, cargo handlers, truckers, carriers and ground handlers one shared online portal in place of fragmented, manual information exchange, with better information sharing, advance planning and truck scheduling. MIA says trucks now often arrive with limited information about arrival times and cargo types. MIA handled a record 3.4 million US tons of freight in 2025, with an average of 190 cargo-only flights and more than 1,600 truck trips a day. Based on what it calls modest estimates, including two hours saved per truck turnaround, MIA says full adoption could save up to $250 million a year in operating costs across its cargo supply chain.

whyItMatters: Trucks that show up unannounced pile up at the cargo warehouse door, and every hour a truck waits is labor and dock space you are paying for. Knowing what is arriving and when lets a cargo handler staff the dock and stage freight ahead of time, so more shipments move per shift. If you handle freight at an airport building a community system, sign up early and ask which data you have to provide and who can see it.
